area: privacy / client PII in published source

An earlier pass had already seeded reClients empty with the comment 'a client name shipped inside published HTML is a disclosure, not a placeholder' - but missed these, because they sat in a data array behind a FUB label rather than in prose. This is exactly the data-not-prose miss class the brief warned about.

fix: Removed with the whole FUB-only card (policy row: 'the frozen 90-day FUB lead card' -> remove). Post-edit scan for name literals matching '["Firstname L.",' returns 0, and the file now contains 0 email addresses of any kind.

area: identifiers carrying saved state / external contract
finding: Five 'fub' identifiers survive in the showings block and were deliberately NOT renamed: the c.fub client property, the shNewClientFub input id that reads it, clientFub in the queued sync payload, and the literal sync-target id "fub" in targets = ["gcal", "fub"]. These are persisted into the showingSchedule and showingSyncRequests localStorage documents (up to 200 queued requests) and the target id is consumed by Steven's showing-sync task on the Mac. Renaming them here would orphan any saved client CRM link and hand the Mac task a target id it has never seen, with no way to verify the other side from this page.
evidence: isa-portal.html lines 4494, 4531, 4589, 4602, 4603. Nothing in the file reads targets back, so the only consumer is external. All associated user-visible text already reads Lofty/CRM: the input placeholder is 'Lofty lead link (optional)', the client row link renders 'CRM record', the copy-out text reads '(CRM link: ...)'.
fix: Kept per FUB-POLICY.md identifier rule ('a localStorage key that carries saved state must NOT be renamed silently - keep the key, rename everything user-visible, and report it'). Needs Steven: renaming "fub" -> "lofty" as a sync target must be done together with the Mac showing-sync task and a migration for already-queued requests.

Every hit was real prose or real code and every one was adjudicated individually. The longest lines in the file (2,098-4,840 chars) are chat preambles and prose, not encoded assets.
